newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says cancels Bre-X's contract bids.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says cancels Bre-X's contract bids.

text.p: Indonesia's government cancelled parliamentary approval of an application for contracts of work by Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd for the huge Busang gold find, one of the world's richest, Mines Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana said Wednesday .
"We cancel it. The Bre-X contract of work will be processed from the beginning," Sudjana told reporters following a marathon parliamentary commission hearing.
The cancellation was the latest twist in a drama over the Busang find, estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold worth more than $21 billion.

The secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, Umar Said, told the hearing the government was checking with the Indonesian Capital Markets Supervisory Agency, Bapepam, on whether Bre-X had misrepresented its status on Busang to the New York Stock Exchange.

"We have obtained a series of documents through our lawyers that show that Bre-X said it owned Busang ll and lll," he said. "Maybe that was meant to push up the price of its shares. We are checking with Bapepam to see if this is criminal," Umar said.

The Indonesian government has been pushing Alberta-based Bre-X and the big Canadian mining company Barrick Gold Corp. to form a 25-75 partnership, respectively, to develop Busang. The government also wants a 10 percent stake in the find.
Bre-X has yet to complete a deal with Barrick because it needs shareholder approval.

The company has a contract of work for the Busang I area of the property on Borneo island, but Busang I contains only an estimated 2.6 million ounces of gold. The bulk of the precious metal is in two adjoining lots, Busang II and III, for which it still needs contracts of work to explore and develop.
Parliamentary approval is the first step in the process of granting contracts of work.

Bre-X had received the parliamentary go-ahead for its Busang II and III contracts of work in July and approval from the Investment Ministry in September. But they were then held up as a result of a dispute over ownership of the property.
Sudjana earlier told the commission that processing of the application for contracts of work by Bre-X was suspended because it did not meet administrative conditions.
He said in a written reply to the commission that the government had detected "bad intentions" by Bre-X, saying it had amended its contract of work when registering with the New York Stock Exchange.
Sudjana said Bre-X had also failed to inform the government and seek its approval when it bought an 80 percent stake in Busang I.

Umar told the commission that in the transfer of share documents, Bre-X Chairman David Walsh had declared himself an Indonesian citizen with a Canadian passport. "... The intention seems to be not good," Umar said.
"The document says David Walsh, Indonesian citizen ... holder of Canadian passport," he said.
Umar reiterated that Bre-X and Barrick had informed him on Dec. 4 that they had completed a deal to develop Busang.

"Bre-X and Barrick have also agreed not to include any new players in the project," he said. "Bre-X has asked for time to get its shareholders' approval over its partnership with Barrick, and the government has taken note of the request," he added.
